Summary: Untrusted code cloned and executed in build

Evidence (line 10):

```
git clone https://github.com/Supreeeme/xwayland-satellite.git
cd xwayland-satellite

cargo build --release
chmod +x ../target/release/xwayland-satellite
cd ..

cp xwayland-satellite/target/release/xwayland-satellite ${APPDIR}/usr/bin
```

Details:

The script downloads and executes code from an external, unofficial repository (`https://github.com/Supreeeme/xwayland-satellite.git`) that is not the official upstream for the `wayvr` project. This introduces a supply-chain risk, as the repository is under a personal GitHub account (`Supreeeme`) and not affiliated with the official project maintainers.

More critically, the script builds and copies `xwayland-satellite` into the AppImage without verifying its source, integrity, or authenticity. The use of `git clone` without a pinned commit allows for mutable, unchecked code to be included at build time. This pattern enables a potential attacker to inject malicious code into the binary after the fact by modifying the remote repository.

Such behavior deviates from standard packaging practices and introduces unverified, executable code into the final artifact, which could lead to backdoors or data exfiltration.
